cards.question: How does RwLock access differ from Mutex?
cards.answer: A Mutex always takes exclusive access. An RwLock allows one exclusive &mut T or multiple shared &T references.

cards.question: When is an RwLock a good fit?
cards.answer: For data that is read frequently but written to infrequently.

cards.question: What is RwLock a thread-safe version of?
Which Deref traits do the RwLock guards implement?
cards.answer: RwLockReadGuard implements Deref only. RwLockWriteGuard implements both Deref and DerefMut.

cards.question: Why wrap an RwLock in Arc for unscoped threads?
cards.answer: So the reference can be moved to other threads.

cards.question: Why can scoped threads share an RwLock without Arc?
cards.answer: A scoped thread finishes before the main function ends, so the lock can be dropped after the scope.
